newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria stock market stagnates in August.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria stock market stagnates in August.

text.p: No corporate issues traded for a fourth week in a row on the Bulgarian stock market because investors eyed other investments, brokers said on Friday.
"Brokers and investors alike shy away from corporate stocks which are deemed low-yield and illiquid," said one broker.
Traders said investments in treasury paper and foreign currency were more attractive at the moment.
The lev has steadily declined against the dollar throughout August, falling to a fresh low of 213 per dollar on the domestic interbank market on Friday from around 187 at the beginning of the month.
Cumulative annual yield of coupon treasury bills ranges between 165 and 194 percent now, under the current historic high main interest rate of 108 percent.
Only the Sofia Stock Exchange (SSE) operated this week after the Bulgarian Stock Exchange (BSE) went into a summer recess on August 5 until September 2.
Investors struck repo deals in treasury paper on the SSE where weekly repo turnover fell to 2.606 million levs from 3.264 million levs last week.
The 13-share Reuter All Bulgaria Stock Exchange Index (RABSI) closed at 41.31 points, unchanged from last Thursday.
* RABSI calculated on daily basis since February 1, 1994
